summary.title: Toren
summary.pov: Third-person limited (focalized through Toren). The narrator is an omniscient observer who knows the internal state of Rook and Tull but strictly filters all descriptions, sensory details, and emotional weight through Toren's immediate perception. Toren sees what he can see; his confusion mirrors the reader's.
summary.synopsis: Rook interrogates a captured man (Tull) on a road at night regarding past atrocities (Homura valley, Lowry Bend). Rook discovers Tull was responsible for killing his mother and brothers. Despite having Tull under physical control with a knife to the throat, Rook chooses not to kill him when an enemy assault begins from the north bank. Instead, he uses magical energy (the 'span of brick') to hold back forty men while being speared through the back by an assassin on the sluice wall. He survives long enough for his company to retreat across a bridge/arch before collapsing.
summary.openingState: Tull is pinned under Rook's knee; Toren watches from ten feet away, hands shaking. The atmosphere is tense, cold, and quiet except for burning reeds. Status: High tension, low movement.
turningPoints: Rook realizes the specific identity of his mother's killers (Lowry Bend) vs. Homura; Tull admits to both but frames Lowry as a mistake rather than malice.
Dessa and Wyck signal an enemy assault on the north bank while Rook holds Tull at knifepoint.
Rook chooses defense over vengeance: he lifts his knife, stands up, and hands Tull over to Hoyle's men instead of killing him.
The magical construct appears; Rook is speared through the back but maintains the barrier until the enemy retreats.
Post-battle debrief where Rook admits he did not choose mercy out of philosophy, but because his 'hands moved' before his mind could decide.
summary.closingState: Rook is critically wounded (rasp hole under ribs, spear through back), sitting on the arch crown. He has exhausted all magical reserves given to Senna earlier. The company is retreating; Tull is gone with Hoyle's men. Rook tells Toren he cannot answer whether he would do it again until a year later.

characters.name: Rook
characters.vocalBehavior: Low register, flat affect, conversational pressure. No rising pitch even in crisis. Rhythm is deliberate and clipped. Status: Absolute authority but physically failing. Reserve: High; he speaks to explain his actions rather than justify them emotionally.

characters.name: Tull
characters.vocalBehavior: Resigned, matter-of-fact. Describes atrocities as 'trade' or 'bad contracts.' No begging, no anger until pushed on the Lowry Bend grievance. Tone: A man conducting business at the end of a long day.

characters.name: Toren
characters.vocalBehavior: Internal monologue is frantic; external speech is hesitant and questioning ('Why?'). He represents the audience's moral confusion. His physical state (shaking hands, running) drives the action cadence.

characters.name: Dessa
characters.vocalBehavior: Projected voice ('pitched a call'), clear and urgent but not panicked. High volume over distance.

terms: Homura: A valley with wire round it; site of a contract.
Lowry Bend: Location of an ambush where Rook's family died.
The span/brick: The magical construct holding back forty men. Described as 'not a wall, not a light' but a physical obstruction.
summary.actionCadence: Slow interrogation (tense stillness) -> Sudden violence (knife insertion) -> Immediate shift to tactical urgency (enemy signal) -> High-speed combat run (Toren's sprint) -> Static magical hold under fire -> Collapse and slow dialogue.
summary.emotionalRegister: Restraint is the dominant mode. Rook suppresses rage; Tull suppresses fear. The emotional peak is not a scream but a quiet admission of lack of choice ('my hands moved before I did').
narrationRisks: The description of the magical construct must be delivered with absolute conviction, avoiding any hint of fantasy 'fluff' or wonder; it is treated as a physical fact by Toren.
Do not over-act Rook's pain. He speaks through his injuries without complaint until he collapses physically.
carryForward: Rook is critically wounded and will be carried on the cart for days; his leadership capacity is now purely verbal/mental.
The company has lost its magical anchor (Senna's flask) and Rook's reserves; they are vulnerable during retreat.
Tull is alive but separated from Cinder Company, creating a loose end regarding future retribution or intelligence.
